Produced by Art East Films, the film stars Oljas Dalelkhan, Rustem Zhanyamanov, Shynar Zhanisbekova, Olga Landina, Akif Petrov and Madina Yesman.
Variety had the chance to interview director Ayana Nurdinova ahead of its world premiere in San Sebastián.

Ayana Nurdinova: I can partly agree that “Mugalim” is a semi-autobiographical story. The main source of inspiration was my own school in the small city of Taldykorgan in southeastern Kazakhstan. articles.title: ‘Resident Evil movies? I’ve never seen one’: Weapons director Zach Cregger on resurrecting the beloved zombie franchise
articles.summary: Raised on punk, alt-comedy and the church, Cregger’s Lynchian approach to horror is anything but typical. After two wildly original hits, his pivot to a 30-year-old video game has caused a storm among protective fans.
body: Even if Cregger had not had a box-office smash that crossed over into awards contention, there would still be an atmosphere of hushed expectation around his next move. Both Barbarian and Weapons addressed hot-button issues – sexual assault and school shootings, respectively – while resisting easy interpretation. Both, too, started out seemingly heading in one narrative direction, before thrillingly careening off elsewhere. Thus, with just two features, Cregger had established a reputation for totally terrifying, utterly unpredictable and – most importantly – genuinely original movies.

Yet the real shocker from this nascent horror auteur is still to come. For his third film, Cregger has taken inspiration from existing intellectual property – or IP, those two little letters bound to strike fear into the heart of even the most stoic cineaste. Zach Cregger has made a Resident Evil movie.

articles.title: Box Office: ‘Resident Evil’ Breaks Franchise Records With $60 Million Opening Weekend
articles.summary: “Weapons” director Zach Cregger has electrified the box office again, this time with his take on “Resident Evil.” His reboot of the ’90s zombie video game has collected $60 million in its opening weekend.
body: In the new “Resident Evil,” Cregger reunites with “Weapons” actor Austin Abrams, who stars as a medical courier who fights through a viral outbreak of infested monsters in Raccoon City. Reviews and audience reception –“Resident Evil” has a 96% on Rotten Tomatoes and “B+” grade on CinemaScore exit polls — should continue to fuel the movie in the coming weeks.

As this weekend’s only major release, “Resident Evil” easily topped the domestic box office. Last weekend’s champion, “Practical Magic 2,” slid to second place with an estimated $11 million from 4,163 theaters, a rough 65% decline from its disappointing $30 million debut. The movie has earned $49 million in North America to date. Warner Bros. spent a substantial $75 million to produce the second “Practical Magic,” which will struggle to get out of the red in its theatrical run since theater owners get to keep half of ticket sales.

articles.title: ‘Backrooms’ Surpasses $400 Million at Global Box Office
articles.summary: “Backrooms” has hit $400 million at the global box office, a remarkable benchmark for the low-budget indie sensation. After nearly four months on the big screen, “Backrooms” has generated $197.5 million domestically and $202.57 million internationally for a worldwide tally of $400.09 million.
body: Among other records, “Backrooms” is by far A24’s highest grossing movie of all time, towering above the prior high-water mark set by “Marty Supreme” with $192 million. It also delivered the indie studio’s biggest debut with $81 million domestically and $118 million worldwide, more than tripling the domestic record previously held by Alex Garland’s 2024 thriller “Civil War” with $25.5 million. And Parsons, who was 20, became the youngest filmmaker with a No. 1 film at the box office, overtaking the benchmark held by Josh Trank, who was 27 when 2012’s “Chronicle” launched in first place with $22 million.

Outside of the United States and Canada, the highest-grossing territories for “Backrooms” were China with $27.8 million, Mexico with $17.8 million, the United Kingdom with $17.6 million, Australia and New Zealand with $12.3 million and France with $12.2 million.

articles.title: Paramount Settlement Talks With State AGs Reach Critical Stage as Merger Opponents Rally and Urge Rob Bonta ‘Do Not Cave’
articles.summary: Paramount Skydance is moving closer to the finish line of its yearlong pursuit of Warner Bros. Discovery as the company’s weekend settlement negotiations with the state attorneys general reach a critical stage.
body: The sides were expected to be in communication Sunday but will pause by evening for the Yom Kippur holiday if the sides have not yet come to an agreement.

As talks between the two sides continue — with the expectation that the situation could come to a head as soon as Sunday night — antimerger activists are planning a series of rallies in Oakland, Los Angeles and New York.

California Attorney General Rob Bonta has demanded “structural remedies” as part of the agreement, but rumors have indicated that his office may agree to something that falls well short of that. The Wall Street Journal, citing unnamed sources, reported Friday that the deal might include operating the two studios “separately for a period,” rather than immediately combining them.

But David Ellison, the CEO of Paramount Skydance, has already agreed to separate operations in some form. In a Feb. 28 letter to Sen. Adam Schiff and Rep. Laura Friedman, two California Democrats, Ellison wrote: “my promise to you is to build a stronger Hollywood, by keeping both of these legacy studios operating separately, thereby preserving and potentially increasing jobs.”

articles.title: Strictly returns with new hosting trio as celebrities find out dance pairings
articles.summary: Emma Willis, Josh Widdicombe and Johannes Radebe take over from long-running presenting duo Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman.
body: Strictly Come Dancing has returned to the small screen for its 24th series, in a new era for the show with a revamped presenting line-up.
An average of 5.3 million viewers tuned in on Saturday with a share of 49.2% of the overnight ratings, which was 7% up on last year, and it remained high on iPlayer's most popular chart on Sunday.
Broadcaster Emma Willis, comedian Josh Widdicombe and former Strictly professional Johannes Radebe made their presenting debut, taking over from Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman, who left last year.
Famous faces including actress Melanie Walters and former England footballer Shaun Wright-Phillips stepped on to the ballroom floor for the first time.

articles.title: Inside the Star-Studded Opening Night of the Lucas Museum: “A New Institution Is Being Born”
articles.summary: George Lucas and Mellody Hobson celebrated their new L.A. museum with the help of Harrison Ford, Leonardo DiCaprio, Oprah, Steven Spielberg, Christopher Nolan, Kim Kardashian and many more.
body: Before the new Lucas Museum of Narrative Art opens to the public on Tuesday, George Lucas and his wife, Mellody Hobson, threw an opening night celebration that will go down in the Hollywood history books.

Queen Latifah, a close friend of the couple, opened the evening as she told the crowd of stars, “Nobody gets to go to a night like this. No one was in the room when the doors opened at the MoMA, or at the Louvre in 1793, or the Met… so we’ve got to feel the gravity of this moment because this is enormous. When you look around, your inclination may be to catch up with friends tonight; we’re all artists in awe of each other, but I implore you to soak this in. Allow these artists to speak to you.”

Architect Ma Yansong spoke briefly before Hobson took the stage, as she teased, “If your husband or spouse comes home and says they want to build a museum, I suggest your response is a hard no.” She explained, “I used to joke with George that at home, one of my jobs as his wife was to serve as a pair of gravity boots; I’d say, ‘George, stay with us,’ as I tried to hold him down. But this time, he pulled me up with him.”

articles.title: ‘Forgotten Island’ Review: Dreamworks Animation’s Latest Celebrates Filipino Folklore With Dazzling Wit and Imagination
articles.summary: The voice cast for this tale of friendship, heritage and growing up includes H.E.R., Dave Franco, Liza Soberano, Jenny Slate, Manny Jacinto, Dolly de Leon and Jo Koy.
body: There’s so much going on thematically and visually in DreamWorks Animation’s new effort that audiences may have a hard time keeping up with it. But that’s all to the good for this rare example of original animated storytelling in a sea of IP and sequels. Utilizing elements of Filipino culture in its wildly imaginative storyline about two friends transported to a mythical land, Forgotten Island marks another winner for directors-screenwriters Joel Crawford and Januel Mercado, who previously punched above their weight with 2022’s Puss in Boots: The Last Wish.

The two girls’ friendship, marked by matching charm bracelets, is tested years later after graduating high school. Lola has died, Jo is working none too successfully at a fast-food restaurant, and Raissa is preparing to leave the country to attend Caltech and pursue her dream of working for NASA. During their last night together, they pass through a magical portal and find themselves on the fantastical island of Nakali that Lola had told them so much about.

articles.title: Matthew Rhys' sister 'so proud of him' after historic Emmy wins
articles.summary: Rhys, from Cardiff, became the first person to win two lead acting Emmy prizes in one night.
body: The sister of Hollywood actor Matthew Rhys said her family had been "pinching ourselves all week" following his historic Emmy success.

His older sister Rachel Evans, who accompanied Rhys to the ceremony in Los Angeles, said she was starstruck seeing Hollywood royalty at the event, and revealed that she and her brother called their parents afterwards, who were sat at home in their dressing gowns.
Speaking to Lucy Owen on BBC Radio Wales, Evans said watching Rhys win the awards was "an experience I will never ever forget or probably match".
She said that as the "bossy" older sister, she told him that morning that he needed to prepare, adding: "If you win, you cannot wing it."

articles.title: Silo Series Author Hugh Howey Loves These 2 Apple TV Sci-Fi Shows
articles.summary: Hugh Howey is a much bigger name now thanks to the TV adaptation of his Silo books, but he's just as much a fan of Apple TV's other hit sci-fi series.
body: Apple TV has, perhaps without trying, become one of the 2020s' best sources for high-concept, big-budget sci-fi television. It was the first streamer, for instance, to finally make a TV series adaptation of Isaac Asimov's "Foundation" stories, a towering achievement. Apple TV is also home to the real-time alien invasion show "Invasion" and "Dark Matter," which Blake Crouch created based on his own novel. That's on top of the dystopian series "See" and the much-celebrated "Pluribus," in which nearly every human on Earth becomes part of a mass consciousness due to an alien virus.

Among the platform's bigger successes, however, is "Silo," created by Graham Yost and based on the "Silo" books by Hugh Howey. The show takes place long after an unknown cataclysm has forced humanity to move underground into giant, 144-level silos. Indeed, so much time has passed in these silos that seemingly no one remembers what even happened that forced them to move there in the first place.

articles.title: Ed Sheeran admits 'mistakes' at first show since Macklemore controversy
articles.summary: The singer spoke about Israel and Gaza after Macklemore was dropped from his tour for making pro-Palestinian remarks on stage.
body: The singer began his concert in Philadelphia by addressing the controversy that has since engulfed the tour and prompted all of his support acts to quit.

"I never wanted to be an activist musician, but this has put me in the middle of an important and passionate argument about free speech and the most complex political issue on the planet," Sheeran said.
He described the 7 October 2023 Hamas-led attacks as "horrific" and called the situation in Gaza "unjustifiable".
The singer has said the decision to drop Macklemore was made by his promoters, not him. The row has seen ticket prices drop and sales decline for the remaining US leg of his Loop Tour.
